discoveries.headline: The 1841 Royal Kalendar, printed page 212, lists John Fitzmaurice as a Junior Clerk under the Surveyor General, between Hy. King and Anty. Harvey.

source.text: The Royal Kalendar, 1841, printed page 212, Internet Archive identifier royal-kalendar-1841

discoveries.imageAlt: 1841 Royal Kalendar, printed page 212, Junior Clerks under the Surveyor General, with the name John Fitzmaurice boxed
discoveries.changeNote: The 1841 appearance had been read only from the scanned text. The page image confirms it.

discoveries.headline: The GRO death index on FreeBMD has no John Fitzmaurice death registered in 1841 or 1842.

source.text: FreeBMD transcription of the GRO death index, searched 26 November 2026

discoveries.changeNote: Those are the years in which he left the Surveyor General clerk list, between the 1841 and 1842 Royal Kalendars.

discoveries.headline: A John Fitzmaurice death was registered in the December quarter of 1840 at Bloomsbury, volume 1, page 74. No age is in the index.

source.text: FreeBMD, Deaths December quarter 1840, Fitzmaurice, John, Bloomsbury 1 74

discoveries.changeNote: This may be John the Ordnance clerk if the 1841 Kalendar was compiled before December 1840. It is not proved.

discoveries.headline: The 1830 Dublin Ordnance Civil Branch clerk lists at Lower Castle Yard, printed pages 109 and 110 of Watson's Almanack, name no Fitzmaurice.

source.text: Watson's Gentleman's and Citizen's Almanack, 1830, printed pages 109 and 110, Internet Archive identifier gentlemanscitize00wats_0

discoveries.imageAlt: 1830 Watson's Almanack, printed page 109, the heading Ordnance, Civil Branch, Office, Lower Castle Yard, boxed
discoveries.changeNote: Robert Thomas still married in 1833 as of the Ordnance Office, Dublin. He is not in this 1830 clerk list.

discoveries.headline: The 1832 Watson's Almanack, printed page 110, lists the Dublin Ordnance Civil Branch clerks at Lower Castle Yard and names no Fitzmaurice.

source.text: Watson's Gentleman's and Citizen's Almanack, 1832, printed page 110, Internet Archive identifier gentlemanscitize00wats_1

discoveries.imageAlt: 1832 Watson's Almanack, printed page 110, the heading Ordnance, Civil Branch, Office, Lower Castle Yard, boxed
discoveries.changeNote: This is two years later than the 1830 lists already on the site, and still before Robert Thomas married in October 1833 as of the Ordnance Office, Dublin. F. A. Jennings is still on the list.

discoveries.headline: A Sun Fire Office catalogue entry dated 25 November 1830 names John Fitzmaurice, gentleman, of 33 Holmes Street, Charles Street, Commercial Road.

source.text: The London Archives, Sun Fire Office policy register, MS 11936/524/1115343, catalogue entry only, not digitised

discoveries.changeNote: The original policy book has not been seen. The address fits the Mile End and Whitechapel area where John's children were baptised. Identification with the Ordnance clerk is probable, not proved.

discoveries.headline: A Sun Fire Office catalogue entry dated 21 January 1834 names John Fitzmaurice, gentleman, of 27 Old Mint, opposite the Irish Barracks, Tower Hill.

source.text: The London Archives, Sun Fire Office policy register, MS 11936/536/1168890, catalogue entry only, not digitised

discoveries.changeNote: The original policy book has not been seen. Tower Hill stands next to the Board of Ordnance at the Tower, where John was a clerk. Identification with him is probable, not proved.

discoveries.headline: The 1904 baptism register of the Ascension, Balham Hill, names Baron Reginald as the son of Edward Dixon and Edith Madeline Fitzmaurice, of 29 Cathles Road.

source.text: Parish of the Ascension, Balham Hill, baptism register, page 76, entry 604, 21 August 1904. Ancestry collection 1558, image 101 of 270.

discoveries.imageAlt: Baptism register of the Ascension, Balham Hill, page 76, image 101 of 270, entry 604 Baron Reginald Fitzmaurice boxed
discoveries.changeNote: The father is described as a civil engineer. No date of birth is written. With the 1911 census, this raises the link from Edward Dixon to Reg from probable to fact.

discoveries.headline: A John Fitzmaurice, aged one and a half, was buried at St Giles in the Fields on 15 December 1840, so the December 1840 Bloomsbury death is not the Ordnance clerk.

source.text: Bishop's Transcript, burials, St Giles in the Fields, page 138, entry 1098. Ancestry collection 1559, image 358 of 365.

discoveries.imageAlt: Burial register of St Giles in the Fields, page 138, image 358 of 365, entry 1098 John Fitzmaurice, aged one and a half, boxed
discoveries.changeNote: St Giles and St George Bloomsbury were in the same registration district, so this infant is almost certainly the December quarter 1840 Bloomsbury entry (C0741). The GRO certificate for that entry is now a weaker suggestion, because the age is already in the burial register.

discoveries.headline: Kelly's 1879 Birmingham directory lists Jones and Fitzmaurice, stone merchants, of Tindal Street, Ladywood, and Robert William Fitzmaurice as a stone merchant of that firm.

source.text: Kelly's Post Office Directory of Birmingham, 1879, printed pages 150, 320 and 592 (Internet Archive bub_gb_dO8NAAAAQAAJ, scan leaves n175, n345, n617)

discoveries.imageAlt: Kelly's 1879 Birmingham directory, page 592, Stone merchants, with Jones and Fitzmaurice, Tindal Street, Ladywood boxed
discoveries.changeNote: The entries had been read only from the scanned text (C0745). The page images confirm them; that this Robert William is our ancestor is probable.

discoveries.headline: The same 1879 directory lists Robert William Fitzmaurice among the private residents of Erdington, at a house called Norlands.

source.text: Kelly's Post Office Directory of Birmingham, 1879, printed page 174, Erdington, private residents (scan leaf n199)

discoveries.imageAlt: Kelly's 1879 Birmingham directory, page 174, Erdington private residents, with Fitzmaurice Robert William, Norlands boxed
discoveries.changeNote: A new home for Robert William between the 1871 and 1881 censuses. His widow Fanny Mary later died at Erdington, in 1917.

discoveries.headline: Published histories of the Cliffe Hill granite quarry at Markfield, Leicestershire, say it was first worked in the 1870s by Jones and Fitzmaurice of Birmingham, who stopped in 1881.

source.text: MQP, The History of Cliffe Hill (time line); Annette McGrath, The Rock Quarries of Charnwood Forest, Mercian Geologist 16 (4), page 253

discoveries.imageAlt: Cliffe Hill Granite Quarry, about 1940 to 1948 (Wikimedia Commons, public domain)
discoveries.changeNote: The Fitzmaurice partner was probably Robert William, the stone merchant of Jones and Fitzmaurice in 1879.

discoveries.headline: John Rupert FitzMaurice acquired the Cliffe Hill quarry from his father on 9 May 1891 and reopened it, with Peter Preston as manager.

source.text: Annette McGrath, The Rock Quarries of Charnwood Forest, Mercian Geologist 16 (4), page 253, citing M. H. Billington, Cliffe Hill Mineral Railway (1974); MQP, The History of Cliffe Hill

discoveries.changeNote: Explains why John Rupert was a quarry owner when he proved his father's will in 1895.

discoveries.headline: The Cliffe Hill Granite Company Ltd, of Cliffe Hill, Markfield, was registered on 1 November 1894.

source.text: Grace's Guide, Cliffe Hill Granite Co, citing The Stock Exchange Year Book 1908; McGrath 2007, page 253

discoveries.changeNote: Two independent published sources give the same date.

discoveries.headline: The Cliffe Hill Granite Company bought the freehold of the quarry from its founder, J. R. Fitzmaurice, in 1935, and the company history records his death in 1949.

source.text: MQP, The History of Cliffe Hill, time line entries for 1935 and 1949

discoveries.changeNote: The 1949 death agrees with the GRO index and probate calendar already on the site (died 21 September 1949, Leicester).

discoveries.headline: Cliffe Hill is still a working quarry: Tarmac bought the company in 1965, and today MQP produces up to 4.5 million tonnes of granite aggregate a year there.

source.text: MQP, Cliffe Hill Quarry and Asphalt Plant; MQP, The History of Cliffe Hill; Leicestershire and Rutland HER MLE21759

discoveries.changeNote: Answers what became of the family business.

discoveries.headline: Original photographs of Cliffe Hill Granite Co. Ltd lorries and the quarry, by Leicester photographers, were found for sale on Delcampe.

source.text: Delcampe listings 2519731289, 2563308122 and 2563273214, seen 27 November 2026 (nothing bought)

discoveries.changeNote: The company name on the lorries is certain; that it is the family firm is probable. No family member is shown.

discoveries.headline: Holmes Street, off Commercial Road, where John FitzMaurice probably insured a house in 1830, was renamed Exmouth Street in 1867 and has since gone.

source.text: The Underground Map, Exmouth Street, E1

discoveries.changeNote: Lets the 1830 address go on the map as an area circle.

discoveries.headline: The Irish Barracks stood in the old Mint inside the Tower of London, so John FitzMaurice's 1834 house at 27 Old Mint was probably within the Tower walls.

source.text: Historic England research record, Irish Barracks, Tower of London (1109413)

discoveries.changeNote: Puts the clerk's 1834 home a few steps from the Ordnance offices where he worked.
